claims.text: The ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder is a metastable BCC solid solution.
The ball-milled powder has a high defect density and may contain oxygen contamination.
The proposed SPS window is 950–1000 °C, 30–50 MPa, and 10–15 minutes under vacuum or argon.
SPS at 950–1000 °C activates atomic diffusion sufficiently to overcome the kinetic limitation present below 800 °C.
Diffusion of Mg and Al during SPS nucleates secondary intermetallic phases.
The precipitates will include Mg-rich intermetallics such as Mg2Al3 or Mg-Ti-V-rich phases.
High-temperature SPS causes segregation into an Fe-Co-rich BCC matrix.
The secondary phases form a percolating microstructural network.
The secondary-phase network acts as a diffusion barrier for bulk pore evolution and surface oxidation.
Precipitation hardening and an increased BCC fraction raise the alloy hardness.
SPS-induced pore elimination increases the bulk density.
A continuous MgO/Al2O3 oxide film, with Cr2O3 if trace Cr is present, enhances corrosion resistance.
Al promotes BCC stabilization, and a greater BCC fraction provides a higher hardness baseline in the target alloy.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the BCC solid-solution matrix.
SPS in the proposed window will produce density above 95% of theoretical and Vickers hardness above 400 HV.
The processed alloy will exhibit a corrosion-potential shift to a value above 0.1 V versus SHE.
Above 1000 °C, Mg evaporation causes more than 5 wt% Mg loss, composition deviation, porosity, and reduced hardness.
Below 800 °C, diffusion is insufficient to precipitate the barrier-forming phases and form a dense bulk alloy.
Diffusion-controlled oxidation should exhibit parabolic weight-gain kinetics, a continuous barrier layer, and Mg/Al concentration gradients through the oxide.
Surface-reaction-limited oxidation should exhibit linear kinetics and a discontinuous scale or no distinct diffusion-barrier layer.
